Iowa offensive line named to Joe Moore Award midseason honor roll
The University of Iowa's offensive line was named to the Joe Moore Award midseason honor roll on Oct.14 by the awards committee. The group has contributed significantly to team statistics this season as semifinalist selections approach.
The University of Iowa’s offensive line was named to the midseason honor roll for the Joe Moore Award, the awards committee announced on Oct. 14. The Joe Moore Award recognizes offensive line units that demonstrate toughness, effort, teamwork, consistency, technique and finishing. It is named after Joe Moore, who is regarded as one of college football’s top offensive line coaches and is notable for being the only major award honoring a unit rather than an individual.
Iowa’s starting lineup features center Cael Winter, guards Kade Pieper and Leighton Jones, and tackles Trevor Lauck and Jack Dotzler. This group has started every game for Iowa this season and collectively has 56 career starts. Two members of the unit—Lauck and Pieper—were also placed on the Lombardi Award Midseason Watch List earlier in the day.
This season, Iowa has surpassed 200 rushing yards in three games, including a 422-yard performance against Northern Iowa in Week 2—the seventh-highest single-game total in program history. In that contest, three Hawkeyes rushed for over 100 yards each—a feat last achieved by Iowa in 1983. Overall this year, five different players have posted at least one 100-yard rushing game; Kamari Moulton recorded a season-best with 208 yards during Week 6 at Washington.
The Hawkeyes are averaging 31 points per game and generating an average of 403.2 total yards per contest. Their rushing attack accounts for an average of 194 yards per game while allowing just five sacks through six games.
The voting committee will consider these performances as it prepares to announce semifinalists in November and finalists in early December. The winner will be revealed following an annual surprise visit to the selected university later that month.
Iowa previously won the Joe Moore Award in both 2016 and 2025; it is one of three schools—including Michigan and Alabama—to have earned multiple honors. The No. 17-ranked Hawkeyes (5-1 overall; 2-1 conference) are scheduled to play Minnesota (4-2 overall; 2-1 conference) on Saturday, Oct. 24.
